lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is the San Miguel County BOCC, which holds public hearings on three separate Land Use Code amendments Wednesday — including changes to the 'Qualified Owner' definition, a wildfire-areas update, and nonconforming lots, all moving toward formal votes. Also Wednesday, the Telluride Housing Authority Subcommittee takes up a deed-restricted homeowner's request to exceed the 5% capital improvement limit for a $47,000 roof replacement, and Mountain Village's Design Review Board weighs in on three multifamily projects Thursday.

notable.stake: Three Land Use Code amendments up for public hearing and formal vote.
Board decides whether deed-restricted owner can exceed improvement cap for needed roof.
Three multifamily projects face design and conditional-use permit review.
Definition changes to Ouray County Land Use Code could quietly shift what rules allow.
